readings.title: Testing the Bonds of Covenant
readings.subtitle: Elisha refuses to break his commitment as Ěliyahu journeys toward the Jordan.
readings.text:
[2 Kings 2:1] And it came to be, when <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was to take up <dn>את</dn> Ěliyahu to the heavens by a whirlwind, that Ěliyahu went with Elisha from Gilgal.
[2] And Ěliyahu said to Elisha, “Please remain here, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has sent me on to Běyth Ěl.” And Elisha said, “As <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> lives, and as your being lives, I do not leave you!” And they went down to Běyth Ěl.
[3] And the sons of the prophets who were at Běyth Ěl came out to Elisha, and said to him, “Do you know that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is taking away <dn>את</dn> your master from your head?” And he said, “I also know, be silent!”
[4] And Ěliyahu said to him, “Elisha, please remain here, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has sent me on to Yeriḥo.” And he said, “As <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> lives, and as your being lives, I do not leave you!” And they came into Yeriḥo.
[5] And the sons of the prophets who were at Yeriḥo came to Elisha and said to him, “Do you know that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is taking away <dn>את</dn> your master from over you today?” And he said, “I also know, be silent!”
[6] And Ěliyahu said to him, “Please remain here, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has sent me on to the Yarděn.” And he said, “As <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> lives, and as your being lives, I do not leave you!” And the two of them went on.

readings.title: The Chariot of Fire and the Double Portion
readings.subtitle: Ěliyahu is taken up in a whirlwind, and Elisha inherits the physical manifestation of prophetic power.
readings.text:
[7] And fifty men of the sons of the prophets went and stood facing them at a distance, while the two of them stood by the Yarděn.
[8] And Ěliyahu took his mantle, and rolled it up, and struck <dn>את</dn> the water. And it was divided this way and that, so that the two of them passed over on dry ground.
[9] And it came to be, when they had passed over, that Ěliyahu said to Elisha, “Ask what <dn>I</dn> am to do for you, before <dn>I</dn> am taken away from you!” And Elisha said, “Please let a double portion of your spirit be upon me.”
[10] And he said, “You have made it hard to ask, yet if you see me when <dn>I</dn> am taken from you, it is yours; but if not, it is not.”
[11] And it came to be, as they continued on and spoke, that see, a chariot of fire with horses of fire which separated the two of them. And Ěliyahu went up by a whirlwind into the heavens.
[12] And Elisha saw it, and he cried out, “My father, my father, the chariot of Yisra’ěl and its horsemen!” And he saw him no more. Then he took hold of his garments and tore them into two pieces.
[13] And he took up <dn>את</dn> the mantle of Ěliyahu that had fallen from him, and went back and stood by the bank of the Yarděn.
[14] And he took <dn>את</dn> the mantle of Ěliyahu that had fallen from him, and struck <dn>את</dn> the water, and said, “Where is <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Ěliyahu?” And he struck <dn>את</dn> the water, and it was divided this way and that, and Elisha passed over.

readings.title: The Futile Search of the Prophets
readings.subtitle: The sons of the prophets fail to recognize the absolute transfer of YeHoVaH's authority.
readings.text:
[15] And when the sons of the prophets who were from Yeriḥo saw him, they said, “The spirit of Ěliyahu rests on Elisha.” And they came to meet him, and bowed to the ground before him.
[16] And they said to him, “Look, there are fifty strong men with your servants. Please let them go and search for your master, lest the Spirit of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has taken <dn>את</dn> him up and cast him upon some mountain or into some valley.” And he said, “Send no one.”
[17] But they pressed upon him till he was ashamed, and he said, “Send.” So they sent fifty men, and they searched for three days but did not find him.
[18] And they returned to him, for he remained in Yeriḥo, and he said to them, “Did I not say to you, ‘Do not go’?”

readings.title: Restoring the Waters of Yeriḥo
readings.subtitle: Elisha acts as the agent of YeHoVaH to reverse barrenness and bring ecological harmony.
readings.text:
[2 Kings 2:19] And the men of the city said to Elisha, “Look, the site of this city is good, as my master sees, but the waters are spoilt, and the soil barren.”
[20] And he said, “Bring me a new bowl, and put salt in it.” And they brought it to him.
[21] And he went out to the source of the water, and threw salt in there, and said, “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘<dn>I</dn> have healed this water – no longer shall death or barrenness come from it.’</dq> ”
[22] And the waters were healed, to this day, according to the word of Elisha which he spoke.

readings.title: The Curse on the Mockers
readings.subtitle: Absolute justice is extracted against those who mock the authorized agent of YeHoVaH.
readings.text:
[23] And he went up from there to Běyth Ěl. And as he was going up the way, some youths came from the city and mocked him, and said to him, “Go up, baldhead! Go up, baldhead!”
[24] And he turned around and looked at them, and pronounced a curse on them in the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And two female bears came out of the forest and tore to pieces forty-two of the youths.
[25] And from there he went to Mount Karmel, and from there he returned to Shomeron.

readings.title: Multiplying the Widow's Oil
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH provides a miraculous surplus to cancel debt and protect the vulnerable from retributive enslavement.
readings.text:
[2 Kings 4:1] And a certain woman of the wives of the sons of the prophets cried out to Elisha, saying, “Your servant my husband is dead, and you know that your servant feared <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And the lender has come to take <dn>את</dn> my two sons to be his slaves.”
[2] And Elisha said to her, “What should <dn>I</dn> do for you? Inform me, what do you have in the house?” And she said, “Your female servant has none at all in the house except a pot of oil.”
[3] And he said, “Go, borrow vessels from everywhere, from all your neighbours, empty vessels, do not get a few.
[4] “And when you have come in, you shall shut the door behind you and your sons. Then pour it into all those vessels, and set aside the filled ones.”
[5] So she went from him and shut the door behind her and her sons, who brought the vessels to her, and she poured it out.
[6] And it came to be, when the vessels were filled, that she said to her son, “Bring me another vessel.” But he said to her, “There is not another vessel.” And the oil ceased.
[7] So she went and informed <dn>את</dn> the man of <dn>Elohim</dn>, and he said, “Go, sell the oil and pay your debt. And you and your sons live on the rest.”

readings.title: A Son for the Shunammite
readings.subtitle: A righteous household establishes a secure place for the prophet and receives the premial reward of life.
readings.text:
[2 Kings 4:8] And it came to be on a day that Elisha went to Shuněm, where there was a prominent woman, and she took hold of <dn>את</dn> him to eat some food. And it came to be, as often as he passed by, that he turned in there to eat some food.
[9] And she said to her husband, “Look, I know that this is a set-apart man of <dn>Elohim</dn>, who passes by us continually.
[10] “Please, let us make a small upper room on the wall, and let us put a bed for him there, and a table and a chair and a lampstand. And it shall be, whenever he comes to us, let him turn in there.”
[11] And it came to be on a day that he came there, and he turned in to the upper room and lay down there.
[12] And he said to Gěḥazi his servant, “Call this Shunammite woman.” So he called her, and she stood before him.
[13] And he said to him, “Please say to her, ‘Look, you have gone to all this trouble for us. What is there to be done for you? Should <dn>I</dn> speak on your behalf to the sovereign or to the commander of the army?’ ” And she answered, “<dn>I</dn> am dwelling among my own people.”
[14] And he said, “What then is to be done for her?” And Gěḥazi answered, “Well, she has no son, and her husband is old.”
[15] And he said, “Call her.” So he called her, and she stood in the doorway.
[16] And he said, “About this appointed time next year you shall embrace a son.” And she said, “No, my master, man of <dn>Elohim</dn>, do not lie to your female servant!”
[17] And the woman conceived, and bore a son when the appointed time had come, of which Elisha had spoken to her.

readings.title: The Death of the Child
readings.subtitle: The Shunammite woman faces tragedy with active trust, seeking out the man of Elohim.
readings.text:
[18] And the child grew. And it came to be on a day that he went out to his father, to the reapers,
[19] and he said to his father, “My head, my head!” And he said to a servant, “Take <dn>את</dn> him to his mother.”
[20] So he took him and brought him to his mother, and he sat on her knees till noon, and died.
[21] And she went up and laid <dn>את</dn> him on the bed of the man of <dn>Elohim</dn>, and shut the door on him, and went out.
[22] And she called to her husband, and said, “Please send me one of the young men and one of the donkeys, so that <dn>I</dn> hurry to the man of <dn>Elohim</dn> and return.”
[23] And he said, “Why are you going to him today? It is neither the new moon nor the sabbath.” And she said, “It is well!”
[24] And she saddled the donkey and said to her servant, “Drive and go, do not slow down, except <dn>I</dn> speak to you.”
[25] And she went, and came to the man of <dn>Elohim</dn> at Mount Karmel. And it came to be, when the man of <dn>Elohim</dn> saw her at a distance, that he said to his servant Gěḥazi, “See, the Shunammite woman.
[26] “Please run now to meet her, and say to her, ‘Is it well with you? Is it well with your husband? Is it well with the child?’ ” And she answered, “It is well.”
[27] And she came to the man of <dn>Elohim</dn> at the hill, and she took hold of him by the feet, but Gěḥazi came near to push her away. But the man of <dn>Elohim</dn> said, “Leave her alone, for her being is bitter in her, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has hidden it from me, and has not revealed it to me.”
[28] And she said, “Did <dn>I</dn> ask a son of my master? Did <dn>I</dn> not say, ‘Do not deceive me’?”

readings.title: Elisha Restores the Boy's Life
readings.subtitle: The prophet operates as the physical extension of YeHoVaH to breathe life back into the child.
readings.text:
[29] And he said to Gěḥazi, “Gird up your loins, and take <dn>את</dn> my staff in your hand, and go. When you meet anyone, do not greet him, and when anyone greets you, do not answer him. And you shall lay <dn>את</dn> my staff on the face of the child.”
[30] And the mother of the child said, “As <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> lives, and as your being lives, <dn>I</dn> do not leave you.” And he rose and followed her.
[31] And Gěḥazi went on ahead of them, and laid <dn>את</dn> the staff on the face of the child. But there was no voice and there was no hearing, so he went back to meet him, and reported to him, saying, “The child has not awakened.”
[32] And Elisha came into the house and saw the child was dead, lying on his bed,
[33] and he went in, and shut the door behind the two of them, and prayed to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[34] And he went up and lay on the child, and put his mouth on his mouth, and his eyes on his eyes, and his hands on his hands, and stretched himself out on the child, and the flesh of the child became warm.
[35] And he returned and walked back and forth in the house, then went up and stretched himself out on him. And the child sneezed seven times, and the child opened his eyes.
[36] And he called Gěḥazi and said, “Call this Shunammite.” So he called her. And she came in to him, and he said, “Pick up <dn>את</dn> your son.”
[37] Then she went in and fell at his feet, and bowed herself to the ground, and picked up <dn>את</dn> her son and went out.

readings.title: Purifying the Stew
readings.subtitle: Elisha neutralizes biological disharmony, restoring the food supply for the sons of the prophets.
readings.text:
[2 Kings 4:38] And Elisha returned to Gilgal. And the scarcity of food was in the land, and the sons of the prophets were sitting before him. And he said to his servant, “Put on <dn>את</dn> the large pot, and cook stew for the sons of the prophets.”
[39] And one went out to the field to gather plants, and found a wild vine, and gathered wild cucumbers from it, filling the skirt of his garment, and came and sliced them into the pot of stew, though they did not know what they were.
[40] They then served it to the men to eat. And it came to be, as they were eating the stew, that they cried out and said, “O man of <dn>Elohim</dn>, there is death in the pot!” And they were unable to eat it.
[41] And he said, “Then bring some flour.” And he put it into the pot, and said, “Serve it to the people to eat.” And there was no evil matter in the pot.

readings.title: Multiplying the Loaves
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH commands a surplus from the first-fruits, feeding a hundred men with bread to spare.
readings.text:
[42] Now a man came from Ba‘al Shalishah, and brought the man of <dn>Elohim</dn> <dn>את</dn> bread of the first-fruits, twenty loaves of barley bread, and newly ripened grain in his knapsack. And he said, “Give it to the people to eat.”
[43] And his servant said, “What? Do <dn>I</dn> set <dn>את</dn> this before one hundred men?” And he said, “Give it to the people to eat. For thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘Eat and have some left over.’</dq> ”
[44] And he set <dn>את</dn> it before them, and they ate and had some left over, according to the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
